headline: Littler faces three-week gap before World Championship defence
standfirst: Grand Slam exit and a missed Players Championship Finals mean the champion will not play again until the Alexandra Palace opening night on 11 December.
body: Luke Littler will go almost three weeks without a PDC match after his Grand Slam of Darts defeat, with his next appearance due on the opening night of the 2027 World Championship.

The reigning world champion was beaten 10-8 by Jermaine Wattimena in the last 16 at Wolverhampton. Wattimena led 7-2 and 9-5 before Littler hit a ten-darter to close the gap to 9-7 and then pulled within a leg. The Dutchman held firm in the 18th leg with a 77 finish, and ended with a 101.70 average and ten 180s.

The result leaves Littler with no further tournament before Alexandra Palace. He did not qualify for the Players Championship Finals in Minehead on 27-29 November, because that field is drawn from the year-long Players Championship rankings and he entered only two of the season's 34 events.
That makes the build-up unusual for a title-holder. Littler won last year's Players Championship Finals, beating Nathan Aspinall in the final, but this time he will watch the event from home.

His recent major record adds to the picture. He set a record tournament average of 111.04 at the World Matchplay in July, but lost 10-4 to Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals of the World Series Finals, went out in the first round of the World Grand Prix and reached the quarter-finals of the European Championship.

As defending champion he is expected to open the tournament on Friday 11 December, and it will be his first World Championship match in the Great Hall at Alexandra Palace. Whether the break leaves him fresh or short of match practice is the open question.
